subject: GPU pool baseline, commits & measurement methodology
messages:
From: Kyle Mercer <kyle@scaleedge.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@scaleedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We’re getting final sign-off to move to a Dedicated pool for our inference workloads and need two things from Redwood to finalize procurement and budgeting:

1) Baseline throughput guarantee (tokens/sec and requests/sec) per GPU pool sizing option (e.g., 8xA100 / 16xA100), measured at 95th percentile for a 30-day rolling window.
2) Latency SLO targets for p95 and p99 for typical request sizes (50 tokens, 512 tokens) and the methodology you’ll use to validate them in production.
3) Pricing: reserved commit tiers (monthly), corresponding discounts, and an explicit measurement/penalty model for SLA misses.

We have an internal constraint: we need an initial committed baseline that supports at least 50M tokens/day during peak and a burst model for seasonal spikes. Can you provide a proposal with concrete numbers and how Redwood will measure and report against those guarantees?

Also, do you support a hard cap on latency for requests routed to dedicated versus fallback to Hosted? Procurement wants to understand credit calculation if guarantees are missed.

Thanks,
Kyle
Kyle Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, ScaleEdge AI
Procurement: procurement@scaleedge.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Kyle Mercer <kyle@scaleedge.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Priya Raman <priya.raman@scaleedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Kyle —

Appreciate the clarity. I’m attaching a draft commercial worksheet with commit tiers and an initial SOW (SOW_dedicated_v3.pdf) — this is a working draft. High-level answers inline below, and Sergio will follow up with the engineering measurement plan:

- Baseline throughput: we propose three sizing options (small/medium/large) mapped to GPU counts: Small = 8xA100, Medium = 16xA100, Large = 32xA100. For each size we provide a conservative guaranteed tokens/sec at the pool level (95th pct over 30d) plus an expected requests/sec baseline (assuming 75-token average).
- Latency SLOs: p95/p99 targets for 50/512 token payloads are included in the attached SOW. We typically provide p95 <= 60ms (50 tokens) and p99 <= 220ms (50 tokens) on Dedicated when within committed capacity; larger payloads scale up accordingly.
- Measurement & credits: we measure at the pool ingress (token/sec and req/sec) and compute credits when measured availability drops below the guaranteed baseline for > 4 consecutive hours. Credits are prorated to committed monthly fees; full details in the attached pricing matrix.

Next steps: Sergio will add concrete test scripts and measurement hooks (we expose an SLO dashboard and CSV exports). If the numbers look reasonable, I’ll lock pricing and draft a mutual action plan with milestones for provisioning and verification.

Attachments: SOW_dedicated_v3.pdf (draft), commit_pricing_matrix.csv

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Sergio / Marcus —

Looping you both in to confirm the measurement methodology Kyle asked for. Procurement will want concrete scripts and acceptance criteria. Please see the bullets I added below — can you review and update with numbers we can commit to in writing? We should keep the guarantees conservative to avoid credits.

Proposed measurement methodology (draft):
- Measurement point: ingress at pool load‑balancer (token/sec, req/sec) aggregated per 1m interval.
- Baseline guarantee: 95th percentile tokens/sec across 30-day rolling window measured at pool level.
- Latency SLOs: measure tail latencies p95/p99 at request completion (including queueing). Report both cold-start-included and steady-state numbers; guarantees apply to steady-state only (no cold-start).
- Test harness: synthetic load from 3 geographically distributed load injectors, mixed payloads (10%, 50 tokens; 80%, 75 tokens; 10%, 512 tokens).
- Failure/penalty window: credits apply if measured availability < guaranteed for >4 consecutive hours; credits limited to 25% of monthly commit for repeat infra issues, 10% otherwise.

Can you add the explicit tokens/sec numbers for Small/Medium/Large and realistic p95/p99 targets for 50/512 tokens? Also confirm how we handle burst (temporary exceed) and fallback to Hosted.

—Vanessa

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Vanessa —

Below is a concise engineering proposal for the numbers we can confidently guarantee with the current runtime for the A100-based pools. These are conservative and assume KV cache enabled, batching turned on with 40ms batching window, and quantized model variants where applicable. I’m attaching a detailed test plan (latency_test_plan.xlsx) with scripts and expected distributions.

Guaranteed baselines (pool-level, 95th pct over 30d):
- Small (8xA100): 2.5M tokens/sec; ~10k requests/sec (assumes 75-token avg).
- Medium (16xA100): 5.2M tokens/sec; ~20k requests/sec.
- Large (32xA100): 10.4M tokens/sec; ~40k requests/sec.

Latency SLOs (steady-state, p95 / p99):
- 50 tokens: p95 <= 60ms, p99 <= 210ms.
- 512 tokens: p95 <= 420ms, p99 <= 980ms.

Measurement notes and edge cases:
- Cold starts: excluded from SLA windows for first 5 mins after instance scale-up.
- Bursts: we provide configured burst capacity (up to 25% above committed baseline for up to 2 hours) at a nominal overage rate; after burst budget exhausted, requests are routed to Hosted or throttled based on mutual policy.
- Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to Redwood Hosted for requests when Dedicated is saturated; customers can opt-out. Fallback latency is not covered by Dedicated SLA.
- Penalty calculation: credits are computed on a rolling 30-day average shortfall in tokens/sec vs guaranteed baseline; credit granularity monthly, capped as Vanessa outlined.

I recommend we offer ScaleEdge the Medium pool as their baseline given the 50M tokens/day requirement (Medium supports ~450M tokens/day sustained at guaranteed baseline). If they want the Large pool for headroom we can add a tiered discount structure.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Kyle —

Thanks — Sergio’s test numbers are attached and reflected in the updated commercial worksheet. Summary proposal: 

- Recommended baseline: Medium (16xA100) mapped to a committed monthly spend of $145,000 with a 12-month reserved commit. This baseline guarantees 5.2M tokens/sec (95th pct, 30d) and the latency SLOs noted below.
- Discounting: 18% off list for 12-month commit; 22% for 24-month. One-time provisioning fee waived for this deal.
- Burst policy: 25% burst for up to 2 hours included per month; overage billed at 1.8x list.
- SLA credits: credits trigger after >4 consecutive hours below guarantee; credits prorated to monthly commit, capped at 25% for repeated infra issues.
- Measurement & reporting: we’ll provide access to the SLO dashboard and a daily CSV export; we’ll run an initial 72-hour verification before go-live and a mutual acceptance window of 7 days.

Attachments: SOW_dedicated_v3.pdf (updated), commit_pricing_matrix.csv, latency_test_plan.xlsx

Please let me know if these commercial terms map to your procurement requirements and whether you need a formal service level exhibit attached for legal. If ok, I’ll produce a mutual action plan with dates for provisioning, verification, and go-live.

—Vanessa

From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@scaleedge.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Kyle Mercer <kyle@scaleedge.ai>
Cc: procurement@scaleedge.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing & guarantees for Dedicated GPU pool

Vanessa / Kyle —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detailed test plan. Procurement has one request before we sign the 12-month commit: please reduce the guaranteed tokens/sec for the Medium pool by 10% for a trial 60-day acceptance (so our internal ops can validate with our real traffic patterns) with the following conditions:

1) During the 60-day trial, Redwood will not apply SLA credits for any measured shortfall but will provide daily visibility and a corrective action plan if shortfalls occur.
2) After 60 days, if the Medium pool meets the original guarantees, we convert to the full committed baseline and apply the 18% discount retroactively for that period.
3) If Redwood cannot meet the guarantees after 60 days, we retain the right to terminate without penalty and will only be billed for actual usage.

Also, procurement requests a clear DocuSign link to the SOW and a one-page exhibit that outlines the credit calculation example (simple math). If you can produce those two items and the updated SOW reflecting the 60-day trial caveat, we can move to sign-off next week.

Thanks,
Priya Raman
Director of Procurement, ScaleEdge AI
procurement@scaleedge.ai
